notes: Prices in USD per 1M tokens, standard (non-batch) API tier. Tiered-price models record the base (lowest) tier with the higher tier in the model's note field. Retired models excluded; deprecated-but-available models included. Collected Monday 2026-10-19, 5 days after the previous file. The previous file was collected on Wednesday 2026-10-14 after the Monday 2026-10-12 slot was missed; this file returns the series to its Monday cadence, so any change below may have occurred on any day in a 5-day window rather than a 7-day one. Tracked scope follows the set established on 2026-07-16 so week-over-week deltas stay meaningful. The set stays at 54 rows: no model arrived, none left, and no row was replaced. All 54 rows are unchanged on input, output and cache-read price. That is an eighth consecutive collection with no input or output change on the carried set, and no cache-read change follows the Claude Sonnet 5.5 cut recorded on 2026-10-14. One model substitution with no price effect: on 2026-10-17 DeepSeek upgraded the model served under deepseek-flash from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, per the DeepSeek API change log, which states the calling method and pricing are unchanged. The pricing page now names the 1017 version, and the legacy ids deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are served by it at Flash pricing. The pricing page still lists vision, tool calls, JSON output, a 1M context length and a 384K maximum output for deepseek-flash. As with the 2026-09-14 substitution, a caller on a fixed id now receives a different model at the same price, so capability statements about deepseek-flash need rechecking against the 1017 version. The change log reports benchmark gains and shorter task runtime and output length for the new version; those are vendor claims, not measured here. Newly recorded, with no effect on the rows: DeepSeek's pricing page lists standalone Search and Fetch APIs at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests each, and says server-side tool calls made through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code or Codex are free until per-request billing begins at 00:00 Beijing time on 2026-11-01. xAI's pricing page (published 2026-10-10) states that requests to its US regional endpoint are billed at 1.1x the global token rates, currently for grok-4.7 and grok-4.6 only, and describes its server-side tools as 'SpaceXSI provided'; whether the 1.1x line predates 2026-10-10 was not established. Anthropic's pricing page states that inference_geo 'us' applies a 1.1x multiplier to all token categories on Claude 4.6 and later models; it is recorded here for the first time and was not established as new. Anthropic's model deprecations page lists claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 as Active with a tentative retirement date of 'not sooner than October 15, 2026'. That date has passed with no deprecation notice, so the row stays and the model can be deprecated at any time from here. Still observed and still out of the rows: OpenAI's Ultrafast tier for gpt-6-astra ($60.00/$300.00) and gpt-6.1-sol ($12.00/$60.00); OpenAI's 'Cyber models' table, which lists gpt-5.6-cyber ($12.50/$75.00) and gpt-5.5-cyber ($12.50/$75.00) beside gpt-5.6-sol at its standard row price; gpt-rosalind-research and gpt-rosalind-discovery ($5.00/$25.00) under trusted access; OpenAI gpt-5.2 and earlier; Grok 4.7 Fast, available only in Cursor and Grok Build; Gemini Omni Flash (gemini-omni-1.1-flash) and Gemini Omni Flash Preview (video models); Gemma 4 with no paid tier; Google's image, embedding, TTS, video, live and transcription models; Mistral's GLM 5.3 resale ($1.40/$4.40), excluded per the 2026-09-21 decision; and Ministral 3 in three sizes (3B $0.10/$0.10, 8B $0.15/$0.15, 14B $0.20/$0.20). Mistral Large 4 is still at the page's sale price with no end date, and its model page still returned 404 on 2026-10-19, so no context window is recorded. No Gemini API change log entry after 2026-10-13; gemini-3.7-flash and gemini-3.5-flash remain deprecated and routed to gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3.6-flash with no listed price. Dated events ahead, all carried from earlier files: DeepSeek search billing for harness tool calls begins 2026-11-01; OpenAI states gpt-5.6-sol's promotional pricing is available at least through 2026-11-21; claude-sonnet-4-5 retires 2026-11-30; Gemini 4 Argon doubles to $4.00/$20.00 on 2026-12-01; gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3.6-flash double to $1.50/$7.50 on 2027-01-01. Carried statements unchanged this week: Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer the page says produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text, with the exact increase depending on content and workload shape; per-token prices are unchanged, so the eleven affected rows (claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, claude-mythos-5, claude-mythos-5-1) cost more per unit of text than a per-token comparison against a 4.6-and-earlier row shows. DeepSeek peak hours (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) still apply Monday through Friday excluding Chinese public holidays. Anthropic still states the Claude Sonnet 5 $2/$10 rate is standard and that the cancelled 2026-09-01 increase will not occur.
